Someone by the fire nods at the counter. "We pool food here. Keep what you need for the road — the rest feeds everyone, once it's food."

Daniyar spends the afternoon with the small tree with mitten-shaped leaves (three shapes), spicy root smell — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. By evening daniyar is thoroughly, educationally sick. "NOT food," they announce to the fire, pale. "My body told me so." The lesson is learned

Pork is pork. Smoke it; it keeps for weeks. The tusks make excellent awls. It's dead. The carcass is there on the ground — search the body if you want the meat. But you don't know this flesh. Clean it, test it cautiously, or ask someone who knows. And don't leave it long: meat rots where it lies.

Daniyar sets aside time with the Big Loud flesh. Look, smell, touch — then the smallest taste, and wait. Their tongue goes numb. Their stomach heaves. "NOT food," they gasp. "Poison." The Codex notes it in grim letters. You will not make this mistake twice — Daniyar already made it for you.
